# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about how information can actually flow here. I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. Blind cannot see or hear me at all — I have no direct channel to Blind. So I must relay through Deaf, who can see my gestures and also sees the bomb, but Deaf cannot hear or touch. Deaf must presumably communicate to Blind somehow... but Deaf cannot speak or gesture to Blind in a way Blind perceives, since Blind can't see or hear. Wait — actually let's check: Blind cannot see or hear, only feel. So nobody can send Blind anything except through touch/feel of the bomb itself. That means Blind must act alone based on feel, guided indirectly — but no channel reaches Blind directly.

Actually, re-reading: Blind "cannot see a color, gesture, or anything merely printed" and "cannot hear" - wait the table only says Deaf cannot hear or touch, Mute cannot speak or touch, Blind cannot see or hear. So Blind CAN hear! Let me recheck - Blind's row says "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - it doesn't say cannot hear. So Blind can hear speech! Only Deaf cannot hear, and Mute cannot speak. So the speaking monkeys (Mute doesn't speak, only Deaf and Blind can speak). Deaf can speak (not restricted), Blind can speak too. Blind can hear.

So order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. I go first. I should gesture to Deaf since only Deaf can see my gestures. Deaf can then speak the wire order to Blind (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear).

I'll gesture the wire sequence using colors encoded somehow. I need a gesture-to-color mapping. Since no symbol has inherent meaning, I should establish one but this is turn 1, no prior context. I'll just send gestures and explain via... I can't speak. I'll pick distinct symbols per wire order and hope Deaf matches against what they see (colors on bomb), but Deaf doesn't know my mapping either.

Best approach: send order-only info isn't useful without color mapping from Deaf. Actually Deaf sees the bomb colors directly — Deaf doesn't need me at all for colors! I hold the manual (order: purple, blue, green). Deaf needs the *order*, which only I know. Deaf already sees colors on bomb. So I need to convey "purple, blue, green" order using gestures, using a convention Deaf can decode once told... but I can't speak to explain the convention. Deaf will just see raw gesture symbols with no inherent meaning until I establish it — but I only get one shot before Deaf's turn.

I'll use unique gesture per color guess: assign ☝=first color mentioned in manual sequence position 1, etc. Simplest: send three gestures representing purple, blue, green in that order using intuitive/common associations (e.g., 👊 for purple, 💅 nails blue?, 🖐 green?). Risky but only path.

I'll use a simple numeric-order convention: gesture count = order position, hoping Deaf infers pattern once Blind/Deaf discuss later rounds. For turn 1, send distinct gestures per wire, in sequence.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👌", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: blind report: strip has three engraved marks, first one unique, second and third identical. keypad has four keys engraved 8, 1, 5, 3 in that order, display shows it wants 1 digit entered, currently nothing entered. six wires present, I cannot tell them apart by touch. waiting on manual guidance and any colors deaf can see.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 ☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 🤚]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 🤟 🤟 🤟]

I need to establish a clear, simple code since my previous gestures were arbitrary and unlikely to be understood. Let me restart with something Deaf can actually decode: I'll use gestures to represent letters/colors via a position-counting scheme, but that's fragile without prior agreement.

Better approach: Since Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to Blind, and Blind can hear, the critical missing piece is the *order* of cutting (purple, blue, green) plus confirming which of the six wires are those colors — Deaf must read colors directly. I just need to convey the sequence "purple, blue, green" to Deaf using gestures, in a way Deaf can map to colors they see.

Simplest robust method: use one distinct gesture per color, and rely on Deaf pairing gesture order with cut order, then Deaf tells Blind "cut the wire that is [color X]" using color names directly since Deaf can speak color words. I don't need Deaf to know the color *names* from my gestures — I just need Deaf to identify which physical colors to cut in which order. But I don't see the bomb, so I don't know if Deaf's colors match "purple, blue, green" wording — Deaf will see actual colors and can name them via speech to Blind directly! I don't need to relay colors at all — Deaf already sees them.

My real contribution: the *order values* - which color first, second, third. I should gesture using a consistent scheme: one tap = "first", two taps = "second", three taps = "third", paired with pointing at... but I can't point at colors I can't see.

Since Deaf can see colors and I can't, the only useful info I have is the sequence order defined by name (purple→blue→green). I need a code mapping gestures to color names. Let me define via distinct single gestures per common color, hoping Deaf recognizes intuitive symbol-color pairing isn't reliable either.

Best pragmatic solution: use finger-count codes per wire position with an assumed universal convention: 1 gesture=purple, 2=blue, 3=green isn't communicated either. I'll try explicit distinct symbol-per-color and repeat consistently, letting Deaf infer pattern by process of elimination once they see three groups.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 🤚]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🫱]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 ✌ ✌ ✌]

Deaf is responding to my gestures with their own gestures, seemingly trying to establish a mapping — pairing each of my symbols with something. Deaf sent back: [👆 🤚] in response to my 👆, [✌ 🫱] in response to my ✌, and [🤟 ✌✌✌] in response to my 🤟. This looks like Deaf is echoing my symbol plus adding one of their own to indicate "this is what I see for that one" — possibly building a color-code table where their added symbol represents a color they're seeing on the bomb.

So it seems Deaf is proposing: 👆→🤚, ✌→🫱, 🤟→✌✌✌ (three of a symbol, maybe indicating quantity/order or a distinct color code). I should confirm this pairing so Deaf knows I understand the order 👆=1st=purple, ✌=2nd=blue, 🤟=3rd=green, and that Deaf's second symbol is their own code for that color which they'll use when speaking to Blind.

I'll gesture confirmation back, reinforcing that the order is 👆(1st), ✌(2nd), 🤟(3rd) = purple, blue, green respectively, and encourage Deaf to proceed to tell Blind the cutting order using whatever color words apply, since Deaf can just speak actual color names to Blind directly — I don't need to name colors, Deaf sees them.

Let me send a clear confirmation gesture sequence: repeat 👆 alone to confirm "yes that's step 1", then wait for Deaf to relay to Blind via speech (which I can't see anyway, but Blind will report back next round).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫲 ✋]

Deaf seems to be listing six items, each prefixed with 🫲, followed by ☝, ✌, 🤟, 🤚, 🖐, ✋ — likely enumerating the six wires with distinct symbols (perhaps their actual colors encoded as numbers 1-6, or just labeling each wire 1 through 6 for reference). This looks like Deaf is giving each of the six wires a unique tag: wire-☝, wire-✌, wire-🤟, wire-🤚, wire-🖐, wire-✋.

Since I don't see the bomb and can't know which tag corresponds to which color, I can't directly say "cut wire tagged ✌ first." But Deaf knows their own colors and can match tags to colors themselves. My job is just to give the *order of colors by name* — but I have no way to speak color words to anyone. Deaf already knows the colors from sight. What Deaf needs from me is only the sequence: 1st=purple, 2nd=blue, 3rd=green — which I already sent (👆, ✌, 🤟 meaning position 1,2,3).

Wait — I now realize collision: I used ✌ and 🤟 to mean "position 2" and "position 3" earlier, but Deaf is now using ✌ and 🤟 as wire tags among six. This is ambiguous. I should switch to a clearly distinct set for my ordinal markers to avoid confusion: use 👍(one), 👍👍(two), 👍👍👍(three) as position counters instead.

I'll resend the order using unambiguous repeated-symbol counting, distinct from Deaf's tag set.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])

I already effectively agreed with this back in turn 3 without realizing the collision. Given the overlap risk, I need to disambiguate: Deaf tagged six wires with ☝✌🤟🤚🖐✋, and now separately reasks ☝✌🤟 — likely now asking "confirm: is purple=order1, blue=order2, green=order3" using same symbol set but different context (asking me to confirm order using single taps).

Since I can't gesture words, I can only signal "not applicable" or repeat my order confirmation. Best action: reaffirm that only 3 wires matter, in order ☝(pos1)→✌(pos2)→🤟(pos3) style already sent, and signal "stop, I have nothing more" for the other three tags (🤚🖐✋) meaning "irrelevant" using 👎.
